qualifying_findings.source_title: Updates to GitHub Copilot for Slack and Microsoft Teams
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: Publisher page heading shows September 25, 2026 and a 2 minute read.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub says Copilot integrations for Slack and Microsoft Teams can use files, attachments, message links, images, forwarded-message context, channel history, and thread history; created work links back to the originating conversation and includes direct links to resulting work.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Conversation-origin traceability is a practice pattern for source ingest and audit: team-chat context becomes part of the work package, and the resulting issue or task should preserve provenance back to the discussion that authorized it.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: When chat surfaces initiate agent work, local guidance should require durable links from source conversation to generated GitHub work and should treat attachments and forwarded context as captured source evidence.
qualifying_findings.follow_up_notes: Candidate ingest destinations: source-workflows/source-reconciliation-and-routing.md, agent-workflows index or a leaf on chat-to-work routing, and governance-and-risk/ai-code-evidence-packages.md.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Usage metrics API adds pull request review stages
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: Publisher page heading shows September 25, 2026 and a 2 minute read.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub added pull_request_review_times metrics that split human-reviewed PR timing into ready-to-first-review, first-to-final-review, and final-review-to-merge medians and p90s; Copilot and bot reviews are ignored in this release.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI-assisted code review adoption should measure where review latency moves rather than counting review events alone. Separating human review stages from bot review helps teams avoid misattributing throughput changes to AI tooling.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Evaluation pages can use stage timing as an operating metric for AI-assisted review, especially when comparing AI suggestions against human review bottlenecks.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Agentic autofix now uses Copilot Memory
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: Publisher page heading shows September 25, 2026 and a 1 minute read.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub says agentic autofix reviews existing Copilot Memory entries for security-alert context and stores fix patterns as memory for future use; those memories can inform code review and cloud-agent behavior.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Repository-specific secure fix memory is useful only if teams govern what becomes durable memory, how it is reviewed, and whether a past fix pattern applies to a new alert.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Durable memory pages should distinguish approved repository conventions from merely observed fix history, especially for security repairs that may become future agent context.

qualifying_findings.date_evidence: Publisher page heading shows September 25, 2026 and a 1 minute read.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub added an in-product validator for enterprise managed Copilot settings that detects malformed JSON, unsupported configuration, invalid team mappings, and enforcement-blocking errors in managed-settings and team-mapping files.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Policy-as-file only works when malformed settings and team mapping drift are detected before teams rely on them. This is a concrete example of validating AI tool controls as deployable configuration.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Governance pages should treat managed AI settings as code: validate JSON, map teams explicitly, and require confirmation after default-branch changes before assuming enforcement.

qualifying_findings.source_title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to build custom workflows with canvases
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub describes Copilot app canvases as customizable interfaces shared between user and agent; canvas state can be changed through buttons, cards, filters, and controls, and the agent can use the same capabilities to update the interface.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Shared state surfaces can make agent work inspectable and steerable without forcing every interaction through chat. That supports progress telemetry, task boards, review checklists, and human control points as UI state rather than prose messages.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Application-pattern pages can frame canvases as an implementation of bidirectional human-agent state, not as a product page, and compare them with runbooks, dashboards, and progress artifacts.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Keep, Change, Kill: What We're Doing Differently
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: Publisher archive and article entry show September 25, 2026.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The post reports a small code-context benchmark where agentic exploration with read_file/grep/glob scored highest against a pinned Java repository, while compressed or retrieved representations without reliable line spans produced fabricated or unresolved citations; the author marks the RAG row as confounded pending rerun.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local wiki already cares about code retrieval and evidence. This source is useful because it turns context strategy into an auditable harness question: line spans, control audits, printed inputs, non-empty output assertions, and cost instrumentation are part of the practice.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Codebase RAG and context-packing guidance should require verifiable file:line evidence and should record harness defects as first-class eval findings rather than only ranking tools.

qualifying_findings.source_title: GPU Resource Planning for Self-Hosted Agents
qualifying_findings.date_evidence: Publisher page byline and metadata show September 26, 2026.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The article argues that production self-hosted agent stacks should be sized across orchestration, LLM inference, embeddings, vector database, and memory store layers; it says LLM inference and sometimes embeddings need GPU, while orchestration, vector database serving, and memory store are CPU/RAM-bound.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Self-hosting decisions for coding agents should be architecture- and workload-driven, not just model-size-driven. The article is a practice lead for separating inference capacity, orchestration overhead, memory, and compliance planning.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Treat the article as a secondary-practice lead for application harness sizing and adoption economics; verify specific hardware, license, and sizing claims before durable synthesis.
